usage.summary:
I've taken the model's bounds out of the rate limiter, and the gate passed on the first of 4 runs. I didn't change the model or any ratified statement, so only the code and the driver changed.

**The rate limiter (`src/machine.ts`)**
- It's now a `RateLimiter` class, built with `new RateLimiter(capacity, maxWaiting)`.
- `request(api, id, now)` sends the call, queues it, or refuses it. A refusal reports how many tokens were left and how many calls were already waiting.
- `refill(now)` covers one refill period. Each bucket gets one token, which goes straight to its oldest waiting call if there is one. It returns the calls that went out.
- `snapshot()` reads its state out and `RateLimiter.from(snapshot)` makes it again from that state.
- There's no bound constant left in it, no fixed list of APIs and no clock. An API gets a bucket the first time it's called. When a bucket is full again with nobody waiting, it's removed, which means the same as never having been used.
- It keeps only each API's tokens and waiting calls. Sent calls, refused calls, call counts and the clock are no longer in it.

**The driver (`conformance.ts`)**
- It holds the bounds as constants named after the model's: `Apis`, `Capacity`, `MaxCalls`, `MaxTime`, `MaxWaiting`.
- It also keeps the environment's part of each state (sent, refused, made and the clock) and works out each call's id.
- It explores breadth first, rebuilding the limiter from each saved state before every step. It records one run per step, or with `INVARIANT_COUNT` set it writes only `{states, depth}`.

**Tests (`src/machine.test.ts`)**
- I rewrote them for the new interface and kept the original scenarios: the burst, calls waiting and going out in order, refusal with a full queue, and refilling to full.
- I added tests that capacity and queue length really are parameters, and that a snapshot round-trips.
- I removed the old test that explored every state against the bounds. That checking now happens in the driver, which the gate checks against the model.

**Gate result:** TLC explored 19,489 states, 14 levels deep. Every invariant, witness and known bug passed, and so did conformance. The bounds-plus-one state count matched TLC's, and `node --test` passed.

pins.name: Spec
pins.says: The system starts in Init, and every step is a Next step.

pins.name: TypeOK
pins.says: Each API's bucket always holds between zero and its capacity in tokens, and every call is tracked with when it was made and when it went out or was refused.

pins.name: WithinRate
pins.says: Over any stretch of time, an API never receives more calls than its bucket's capacity plus one per refill period in that stretch.

pins.name: FirstInFirstOut
pins.says: Calls to an API wait and go out in exactly the order they were made.

pins.name: NoNeedlessWait
pins.says: A call only waits while its API's bucket has no tokens left.

pins.name: NoCallLost
pins.says: Every call that was made has gone out, is still waiting, or was refused.

pins.name: BoundedWait
pins.says: No more than MaxWaiting calls are ever waiting for the same API.

pins.name: NoNeedlessRefusal
pins.says: A call is only refused when its API's bucket was empty and MaxWaiting calls were already waiting for that API.

pins.name: BurstGoesOut
pins.says: A full bucket's worth of calls can go out immediately at the start.

pins.name: CallWaits
pins.says: A call can have to wait for a token.

pins.name: WaitingCallGoesOut
pins.says: A call that waited can go out once a token refills.

pins.name: BucketRefills
pins.says: A bucket that was spent from can refill back to full.

pins.name: CallRefused
pins.says: A call can be refused because too many calls are already waiting.

pins.name: SendWithoutToken
pins.says: A call goes out even though its API's bucket is empty.

pins.name: JumpQueue
pins.says: A refilled token goes to the newest waiting call instead of the oldest.

pins.name: QueuePastLimit
pins.says: A call is put in the queue even though MaxWaiting calls are already waiting.

pins.name: RefuseEarly
pins.says: A call is refused while there is still room in its API's queue.
